Subject: Quality monitoring & canary plan for clinical notes generator

Hi Rishi / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency and cost numbers looked promising. We’re ready to start the onboarding work for our clinical notes generator (production rollout targeted for mid-September). Before we hand this off to our engineers, we need a pragmatic quality monitoring plan so we can detect regressions early without creating a ton of noise. High level asks: 

- Baseline prompt sets (10-20 prompts per critical intent) and a way to update them as product prompts change.
- Eval harness integration with our CI so model changes trigger a regression test.
- Regression alert rules (thresholds + who gets paged).
- Canary rollout and automatic rollback policy for model updates.

Can you propose an implementation roadmap with owners and an initial timeline? I’ve attached a one-page scoping matrix. Our IT/ops lead (cc’d it-ops@acmehealth.com) will need to review the security/ingress patterns.

Sam
Sam Park
Director, Clinical Apps
Acme Health

Sam — thanks for the clear asks and for the scoping doc. We can absolutely put together a lightweight, testable rollout that covers prompt sets, eval integration, alerts, and an automated canary/rollback path. Proposed starter plan (high level):

1) Prompt set curation (Week 0-1):
   - Marissa will provision a seed prompt set template (10 critical intents, edge cases, hallucination probes).
   - Owner: Marissa Cole (CS) + Acme SME.

2) Eval harness integration (Week 1-2):
   - Integrate Redwood eval runner into Acme’s CI pipeline. Baseline run after every deploy to staging.
   - Owner: Dev Patel (implementation lead).

3) Alerting & thresholds (Week 2):
   - Define regression thresholds (e.g., 10% degradation in rouge/score, precision drop > X). Alerts -> Slack #acme-qmon and create Jira if severity & persistent.

4) Canary & rollback policy (Week 2-3):
   - Canary fraction (5-10% traffic), degrade to 0% and auto-rollback on major regression metric breaches; manual review gate for non-critical regressions.

5) Knowledge transfer & runbook (Week 3):
   - Handoff doc + runbook + scheduled monthly review.

If that timeline looks good I’ll schedule a 60-min kickoff next week and circulate a mutual action plan (I attach a first draft).

Thanks —

Thanks — adding more detail on the eval & prompt set side.

Quick notes:
- Prompt set template: I’m attaching our QMon probe spreadsheet (qmon-probe-template.xlsx). It includes columns for intent, prompt, expected keys in JSON output, acceptance criteria, and severity. Start with 10 intents x 5 edge cases = 50 probes per model.

- Eval harness: recommendation is to use our eval-runner (open-source) with YAML job specs that map to your CI. We’ll provide an integration snippet that runs on staging and posts results back to the Redwood Console / a webhook.

- Metrics we recommend collecting out-of-the-box: exact match on structured fields, BLEU/ROUGE for free text sections, hallucination flag rate, latency p95, and token cost delta.

- Regression alerts:
  * Soft alert: 3 consecutive job failures or a 7% drop in primary metric -> Slack + ticket.
  * Hard alert: >15% drop or hallucination spike > 5% -> Pager to oncall and immediate canary halt.

- Canary/rollback:
  * Canary window = 48 hours.
  * Auto-shift policy: if hard alert fires, traffic shifts from canary to baseline and rollback request is opened to the deploy team.
  * Manual review: if soft alert triggers but noise suspected, we run an adjudication on a sample of prompts before rolling back.

I’ll own the prompt-set seeding and will coordinate a short scoring calibration session with your SMEs.

—Marissa
